one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-04) very likely contains Q3 2026 earnings (most sources say 2026-11-03 pre-market, some say 2026-10-29; not confirmed by the company). Guidance already given: non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 and gross bookings $58.25-60.25B, which consensus (~$0.89) sat slightly above. Uber has beaten bookings and EBITDA guidance consistently, but the last two prints (Feb and Aug 2026) sold off on EPS/guidance misses and AV capex news, and what moves the stock now is AV news (Tesla Cybercab expansion, Waymo) more than quarterly beats. Two things lean slightly positive: insider buying near these levels (CEO ~$10M at ~$71, COO ~$5.3M at ~$76) and a stock near its 52-week low. One leans negative: possible Q4 guide reflecting AV fleet costs. These roughly cancel, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$69.8 with ~11% one-month sigma (35%/3.5 = 10%, plus a little for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (17x skeptic-grown Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $4.98 = $84.7, 40%), FCF yield (7.5% on $9.8B post-AV-capex FCF = $62.0, 30%) and EV/adj. EBITDA (11x on $15B = $79.3, 30%), giving ~$76.

Peer median fwd P/E ~22x (range 8-124x, interquartile ~14-29x). Uber currently trades at 16.8x and 21x non-GAAP vs a 5-yr average near 30x. I keep it near today's multiple, below the peer median, because AV disintermediation puts the terminal value at risk and keeps the multiple down, as it does for Lyft at 8x

Uber today: EV $146.6B / 2026E adj. EBITDA ~$11.4B = ~12.9x trailing-ish, ~11x NTM. Mature marketplaces BKNG 11.7x and EXPE 10.5x (trailing) set the floor; peer GAAP-basis median 24x is not like-for-like

bear.story: Tesla scales Cybercab and Waymo scales on its own app in Uber's top US cities through 2027. Uber cuts Mobility prices or take rate to hold share, AV fleet capex eats FCF, and the multiple falls to ~11x on ~$4.2 EPS. Litigation headlines (MDL common-carrier ruling, FTC Uber One trial Feb-2027, DOJ ADA) add to the pressure.

base.story: Gross bookings grow high-teens and EPS ~20%, but AV fear keeps the multiple near 16-17x. The stock recovers modestly towards fair value as AV trips stay <1% of volume through 2027.

bull.story: Consensus is delivered (~25-30% EPS growth). The AV aggregator thesis gains ground (Waymo/Baidu/others on the Uber app, Tesla's cost advantage proves slow to scale) and the multiple re-rates to ~21x.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is to the median, not outside the range. The one direct ridehail peer (LYFT, 8x) shows how the market prices AV disintermediation risk, and that risk will last through the horizon: Tesla runs unsupervised in 6+ US cities and is rolling out Cybercab, and Uber's own AV supply only scales from 2028 per BofA. Uber is also moving from asset-light to owning fleets ($7.5B), which lowers returns on capital. Against that, Uber's growth (22% bookings) and BBB+/Baa1 balance sheet beat most peers, so I don't go down to Lyft's multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $52 is ~25% below today and ~20% below the 52-week low, about 10.5x current NTM EPS. A level that low would most likely mean something fundamental, not just a de-rating: Mobility gross bookings slowing to single digits, an explicit take-rate cut or price war in US cities against Tesla/Waymo, a large aggregate MDL/FTC settlement, or AV commitments growing well beyond $10B and swallowing FCF.

Mobility revenue grew only 1% in Q2-26 (business-model changes cost 8pts), which obscures underlying take-rate trends
reasoning: Lane: skeptic. I looked for what makes the Buy consensus (51 analysts, avg PT ~$101) wrong on the downside. (1) Competition from AVs is the main bear argument and is real. Tesla runs unsupervised robotaxis in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa and launched Cybercab in Sept-26. Uber fell 4% that day, and Arete downgraded to Neutral ($74) on lower cost per mile threatening take rates. Melius has had a Sell ($73) since Jan-26. The counter-evidence: Tesla fleets are small (hundreds of cars, availability problems per Electrek), AV trips are <0.5% of Uber rides, and Polymarket priced a California Tesla robotaxi launch by June-30 as very unlikely (~97% No; volume not retrieved). (2) Uber's response is to spend $10B+ on AV, ~$7.5B of it on fleets, moving away from an asset-light model. Meanwhile H1-26 operating cash flow grew only ~7% against +33% adj. EBITDA. (3) Credit is not a bear point. Ratings are Baa1/BBB+/A-, and the Sept-26 EUR 4.5bn issue priced at only +69 to +147bp over Bunds, so markets see no solvency stress. Net debt is modest (~$7.3B) against $10B TTM FCF. (4) Litigation: MDL bellwethers produced $8.5M and $5K verdicts plus a common-carrier ruling; the FTC/21-state Uber One case goes to trial Feb-27; the DOJ ADA suit survived a motion to dismiss. Q2 had a $141M legal reserve. All of this is a headline risk, but no single item threatens the valuation. (5) Insiders: the CEO bought ~$10M at ~$71 and the COO ~$5.3M at ~$76, against one small sale (Hazelbaker, ~$2M). That is a contrarian positive. (6) Accounting: GAAP EPS is noisy because of equity revaluations ($1.6B Q2 gain). Mobility revenue growth of 1% reflects business-model reclassification, not lost demand: bookings grew +22%. Valuation: blended fair value $76 (P/E $84.7, FCF $62, EV/EBITDA $79.3), ~9% above spot, with growth and multiples haircut versus consensus. Scenarios: $46 / $77 / $104 at 25/50/25, mean ~$76. For the ladder I used a three-lognormal mixture (bear centre $48, sd 0.30; base $77, sd 0.20; bull $103, sd 0.20). That gives median ~$77, P(>=$70) ~61%, and an overall spread a bit wider than the 35% realized vol, with a fat left tail because AV disruption could be binary. Research limits: the Twelve Data statistics, estimates and earnings endpoints were paywalled, so consensus came from StockAnalysis/MarketScreener via search. Peer EV/EBITDA is trailing GAAP, not forward. Source mix: 16 of 32 sources are in-lane. Excluding the 10 mandated peer-data pages and the basic-fact filings/data pages, 16 of 20 are.
